target_claim: We shall prove that, for any fixed $k,n$ with $n$ having the prime decomposition above, there is a prime $p$, and integer $q$, and a positive integer $m$, such that $pq^m \equiv k\pmod{p_j^{a_j}}$, for every $1\leq j\leq K$.
source_quote: We shall prove that, for any fixed $k,n$ with $n$ having the prime decomposition above, there is a prime $p$, and integer $q$, and a positive integer $m$, such that $pq^m \equiv k\pmod{p_j^{a_j}}$, for every $1\leq j\leq K$.
